data.name: Sohel
data.gender_notes: Sohel is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit word ‘Soham’, meaning ‘I am the Sun’. This name is associated with the radiant and bright nature of the Sun, and the light it brings into one's life. The name Sohel carries the meaning “Sun, Bright, Shining” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Bengali. Parents who choose Sohel usually hope their child will grow to embody sun, bright, shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Sohel belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun, Bright, Shining.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sohel total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sohel holds a rich cultural significance within the Hindu community as it derives from the powerful and revered symbolism of the Sun. In Hinduism, the Sun represents energy, strength, courage, and enlightenment, among other attributes. It's a source of life that shapes and nurtures every being, which is why individuals with the name Sohel are often thought of as possessing these qualities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sohel contains deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of our inner connection to the divine, boundless source of light and consciousness. Soham, which Sohel comes from, holds great importance in Hindu spirituality and is often used as a meditation mantra in various spiritual practices. In this mantra, the practitioner recalls their innate nature as pure cosmic consciousness, the same essence as the life-giving Sun.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sohel, meaning 'sun among the clouds', symbolizes the radiant spirit that shines through adversity. It represents the individual's innate ability to bring light and hope even in the most challenging circumstances.

historical_references.reference: Sohel Khan was a prominent Mughal nobleman during the rule of Emperor Aurangzeb. He was the governor of Bihar and held the title of Subahdar. Sohel Khan played an instrumental role in the Battle of Samugarh in 1666 AD, where he led the Mughal forces against the Maratha and Rajput army led by Jai Singh I. The battle took place near the city of Agra in India.

Sohel Rao was a Maratha military leader who rebelled against the Mughal rule during the late 17th to early 18th century. He was initially a commander under Shivaji, but later declared himself as a king and ruled over a significant part of present-day Maharashtra. Sohel Rao was known for his military prowess and expanded his territory through several battles against the Mughals. He was eventually defeated by the Mughal forces under the command of Bahadur Shah I in 1717 AD.
